title: ColumbiaWalks walking-safety checklist
instructions: Choose the major issue type first. Only related follow-up questions will appear. Answer only the items you can observe, add context in the report details, and attach a photo only when it is safe to do so.

sources.nhtsa_2025: NHTSA Rate Your Walk: Pedestrian Walkability Checklist (2025)
sources.caerphilly_vehicle_safety: Caerphilly County Borough Council vehicle movements and pedestrian safety inspection checklist
sources.florida_srts: Florida Safe Routes to School Walk and Bike to School Day Pre-Assessment Site Checklist

categories.title: Sidewalks, paths & trip hazards
categories.description: Walking space, continuity, condition, maintenance, and comfort.

questions.text: Is there a safe, designated space to walk?
Are sidewalks or separated paths provided where pedestrians need them?
Are walkways and shared entrances wide enough for people to pass safely?
Are sidewalks and walking routes continuous and free of gaps?
Are walking surfaces free of debris, cracks, holes, uneven areas, slippery spots, and other trip hazards?
Are walkways maintained during winter, including timely ice and snow control?
Is the route clean and free of litter or trash?
Does the walking route appear to be regularly used?
Are public seating and weather-shelter options available where they are needed?
Is there adequate shade along the route?
Is traffic noise low enough that the walk feels comfortable?

categories.title: Crosswalks & intersections
categories.description: Crossing distance, signals, markings, traffic control, and pedestrian visibility.

questions.text: Is the crossing distance short enough to cross safely?
Do traffic signals operate often enough and allow enough time to cross?
Are pedestrian walk signals present, working, and accessible to people with low vision?
Are needed crosswalks clearly marked in each crossing direction?
Are crossing points placed appropriately and used as intended?
Are intersections clear of parked vehicles, plants, and other objects that block views?
Are curb ramps present and well maintained at crossings?
Is an adult crossing guard present where one is needed?
Are appropriate stop signs, traffic lights, and vehicle signs present?
Can the intersection safely handle the observed motor-vehicle and pedestrian traffic volumes?

categories.title: Drivers & traffic behavior
categories.description: Yielding, speed, signals, stopping, backing, and aggressive conduct.

questions.text: Do drivers scan the surrounding area before backing up?
Do drivers yield to children and other pedestrians crossing the street?
Do drivers use turn signals and other clear visual cues?
Do drivers travel at a safe speed for the posted limit and current conditions?
Do drivers slow and stop for traffic lights instead of speeding through them?
Do drivers stop at stop signs and red lights and turn cautiously?
Do drivers leave crosswalks clear when stopped?
Are pedestrians free from threatening, harassing, crowding, following, or intentionally aggressive driving?

categories.title: Lighting & sight distance
categories.description: Lighting and clear views between drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

questions.text: Is the walking route adequately lit when used after dark?
Can pedestrians and drivers see approaching traffic clearly at crossings?
Are parking and waiting vehicles kept from blocking sight lines?
Are fences, walls, dumpsters, utility boxes, landscaping, signs, and buildings placed so they do not block views?
Do vehicle routes avoid sharp or blind bends that hide pedestrians?

categories.title: Accessibility & mobility
categories.description: Wheelchair access, detectable warnings, accessible signals, and inclusive pick-up areas.

questions.text: Are routes, crossings, and entrances usable by people using wheelchairs or other mobility devices?
Are accessible curb ramps available where needed?
Do curb ramps have tactile warning strips or another detectable surface?
Are pick-up and drop-off areas safe and accessible for people with physical disabilities?

categories.title: Vehicle routes, parking & site operations
categories.description: Separation, delivery areas, parking, reversing, speed control, and driver management.

questions.text: Are vehicles and pedestrians kept safely separated wherever practical?
Are barriers or railings provided at gates, corners, entrances, and blind spots where needed?
Are traffic routes, entrances, and gateways wide enough for safe shared use?
Is site traffic arranged to avoid congestion that increases pedestrian risk?
Are one-way systems or parking restrictions used where they would reduce conflicts?
Are delivery and loading activities kept in a designated area away from pedestrians and passing traffic?
Are roads and parking areas well constructed, maintained, and free of obstructions or hazards?
Are roads and parking areas maintained during winter, including ice control?
Are roadways marked where needed for right-of-way, no-entry, and other controls?
Are speed bumps, speed tables, surface treatments, or other speed-control measures used where needed?
Are appropriate speed limits posted for site roadways?
Are drivers clearly informed of site rules through suitable safety signs?
Are safety signs clear, consistent, and appropriate for the location?
Has the need for vehicles to reverse, and the distance they reverse, been minimized?
Are reversing areas designated and kept separate from pedestrians?
Are mirrors, cameras, or other aids provided where backing visibility is limited?
Is reversing supervised when site conditions make supervision necessary?
Are visiting and delivery drivers kept away from peak pedestrian periods where necessary?
Are visiting drivers told the rules and controlled or supervised in restricted areas?
Is unsafe behavior addressed and are unnecessary vehicle trips on the site minimized?

categories.title: School arrival, bus & bicycle areas
categories.description: Specialized checks for schools, student drop-off, bus loading, bicycle routes, and school zones.

questions.text: Are students entering or leaving cars protected from moving vehicles?
Does a continuous raised curb separate student drop-off areas from moving vehicles?
Are vehicular and pedestrian signs posted around student drop-off areas?
Does traffic move through the student drop-off area without unsafe congestion or backups?
Are bus driveways separated from pedestrian and bicycle routes by curbs or bollards?
Are bus driveways separated from parent pick-up and drop-off areas?
Where buses double-stack, are students protected when crossing in front of or behind buses?
Is bus-loading traffic one-way and wide enough for safe drop-off and pull-out movements?
Is there a continuous curb and sidewalk from the bus loading zone to the school?
Is the bus loading and unloading zone adequately lit?
Are bicycle routes designated by signs and marked lanes where appropriate?
Are students supervised during school arrival and departure?
Are nonessential vehicles restricted without shifting risk to nearby public streets?
Is a Safe Routes to School approach used to reduce vehicle traffic near the school?
Are school-advance, school-crossing, school-speed-limit, beacon, and parking-control signs provided where needed?
Is there an effective school-focused traffic-safety or enforcement program?
Is a designated school zone clearly identified?
Are school pavement markings present on nearby roadways where needed?

categories.title: Walking practices & overall comfort
categories.description: Observable pedestrian actions and the overall experience of the walk.

questions.text: Can people cross at a crosswalk or intersection where they can see and be seen?
Can people stop and look left, right, and left again before crossing?
Can people use a sidewalk, or face traffic on a shoulder where no sidewalk exists?
Can people complete the crossing within the available time?
Can people cross with the traffic light?
Did the walk feel safe overall?

categories.title: Police & emergency response
categories.description: Optional feedback when police or emergency responders were involved.

questions.text: If police were involved, did their response improve safety at the scene?
If police were involved, was the response timely, respectful, and appropriate?
